name: PADOG
description: Weighted gene set analysis method that down-weighs genes that are present in many pathways. Supports multiple Omics data sources including Ribo-Seq data

parameters.name: use_interactors
parameters.description: Indicates whether interactors from IntAct should be used to extent REACTOME's pathways in the analysis.

parameters.name: include_disease_pathways
parameters.description: Disease pathways in Reactome may lead to a skewed analysis result. Note: Excluding disease pathways currently prevents the visualization of results in the Reactome pathway browser.

parameters.name: max_missing_values
parameters.description: The maximum (relative) number of missing values within one comparison group before a gene / protein is removed from analysis. If no comparison groups are defined (for example for 'ssGSEA', the number of missing values accross all samples is used. Must be between 0-1.

parameters.name: create_reactome_visualization
parameters.description: If set to 'False', no REACTOME visualization is created for the performed analysis.

parameters.name: create_reports
parameters.description: If set to 'True', additional Microsoft Excel and PDF-based reports of the analysis result will be created.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: If set to a valid e-mail address, links to the analysis result (and report) will be sent once the analysis is complete.

parameters.name: reactome_server
parameters.description: This parameter allows the usage of other reactome servers. Available options are 'production', 'dev', 'release'

parameters.name: sample_groups
parameters.description: Specifies the sample property name that holds the sample group information. This parameter should be used for matched-pair analyses (f.e., the same patients before and after therapy). If used, every sample must occur exactly twice, once in each of the analysis groups.

parameters.name: discrete_norm_function
parameters.description: The normalisation function to use for raw RNA-seq read counts and raw Proteomics spectral counts. By default, the TMM normalisation is used.

parameters.name: continuous_norm_function
parameters.description: The normalisation function to use for proteomics intensity data. Note that it is generally advised that normalisation is performed on the PSM or peptide level and not on the protein level.

parameters.name: pathways
parameters.description: A comma delimited list of pathways to include in the analysis. All other pathways will be ignored.

parameters.name: min_size
parameters.description: The minimum pathway size (determined as the number of submitted genes mapped to that pathway) to include a pathway in the analysis.

parameters.name: max_size
parameters.description: The maximum pathway size (determined as the number of submitted genes mapped to that pathway) to include a pathway in the analysis.

name: terapadog
